This game blends creature collection, survival mechanics and exploration wonderfully, and the progression feels pretty good outside of the late game technology point grind. All of the systems, though some can certainly be a pain at first (climate, food decay, weapon repairs), can all be managed reasonably or mitigated somewhat through abilities and items. The base creation, while seemingly limited at first due to the small size of the given building space, takes off once you realize the vertical potential. However, some of the bigger pals clip through tight rooms and areas, which can be a little off-putting at best, and downright criminal at worst. (the pals can get very large)

Overall, while I am not completely finished with the game, I've enjoyed it significantly more than I thought I would, and I absolutely recommend it to anyone who enjoyed Pokémon in the past, as well as anyone else interested.

Movement, fighting and gliding feel clunky and cheap compared to other games. Holding a button while building is unnecessary and annoying (thankfully theres a setting that fixes that). Pal and item switching isnt good either (overall the whole moving and doing doesnt feel as smooth as it should, chopping and mining included). There seems to not be enough information in the mission tab about the thing im supposed to do (I went to fight the first boss and only realised that I'm underleveled after getting easily beaten by it). Other than that the game looks fine. I wouldnt recommend it at the moment though. That said, maybe I haven't played enough to be able to write a proper review, but I probably won't be playing it again, so there's that...
